# czc-v2026.10.27.4 (0.2.18.6)

DeepSeek user billing now follows the official weekday peak 2× catalog rate
when a channel or group only has an empty token stub for the model. Previously
those stubs were treated as custom pricing, so peak-hour user charges stayed at
the off-peak catalog rate while account-cost stats still used the official 2×.

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.27.3

- Treat empty token cards (all price fields unset) as catalog pricing, not as
  operator-custom rates. Official DeepSeek peak 2× applies again.
- Keep real custom cards unchanged: an explicit input/output/cache/image price,
  per-request/image/video mode, fast/flex/reasoning multipliers, time pricing,
  or a priced interval still skips official peak scaling.
- Production already deleted the empty `deepseek-v4.1-flash` card on the
  DeepSeek channel so the running process could bill peak 2× before this
  release. This build prevents the same skip if an empty stub is added again.

## VERSION

`0.2.18.6`

## Upgrade guidance and compatibility

- No database migration, configuration update or API key replacement is needed.
- Group rate multipliers are unchanged. DeepSeek group 84 remains `1.0`.
- Operator-custom DeepSeek prices still do not receive official peak 2×.
- Empty token stubs on other platforms were already catalog-priced for
  non-DeepSeek models; this change only restores DeepSeek peak scaling for
  those stubs.
- Peak windows remain weekday UTC 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00. Beijing weekend
  stays off-peak.
- Build from this exact tag, rebuild the frontend immediately before the
  `-tags embed` server build, and set `main.ReleaseURL` to this origin release.

update-check response reports
`https://github.com/zuchengchen/sub2api/releases/tag/czc-v2026.10.27.4`.

## Rollback

Restore the pre-install binary saved as
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.27.4-<UTC timestamp>` and restart
`sub2api.service`, or rebuild and deploy `czc-v2026.10.27.3` (`0.2.18.5`).
No database or configuration rollback is required. The empty DeepSeek card
was already deleted in production; rolling back the binary does not restore
that card. Verify HTTP 200, version `0.2.18.5` and the previous origin
release URL after rollback.
